newsitem.title: USA: CBOT-CME talks to continue despite European links.
newsitem.headline: CBOT-CME talks to continue despite European links.

text.p: Chicago futures exchanges will continue to work towards unifying operations, despite the separate agreements each exchange recently established with European exchanges ahead of a single European currency, U.S. futures industry sources said.
"I don't see this in any way diminishing that effort," Chicago Mercantile Exchange president William Brodsky told Reuters.
Both CME and CBOT officials said the Joint Strategic Initiatives Committee's focus remained on merging back-office functions, and not on product or contract development.

"The two exchanges will continue to compete for new products, while working together on making our markets efficient and reaching a commonality for our customers," said David Prosperi, a Chicago Board of Trade spokesman.

Between them, the CBOT and CME will eventually offer during U.S. hours long-term Euro-denominated government bonds, short-term interest rate contracts denominated in European currencies, and 10-year French bonds.

Merton Miller, head of the exchanges' joint strategic committee, said the Euro instruments might be able to compete viably with each other within the same time zone since they represent long-, medium- and short-term rates.
"They are going to be at different ends of the spectrum," Miller said.
The CME plans to trade MATIF's 10-year French bond contract and LIFFE's contracts on short-term debt denominated in marks, sterling, the ECU, lira and Swiss francs next year.
The CBOT plans to trade LIFFE's long Euro-denominated debt contract if and when the EMU is implemented in 1999. The CBOT plans to trade LIFFE's German bund contract in May 1997.
Larry Arnowitz, managing director of GNI Inc, said the success of Chicago's linkages with European exchanges would depend on costs, as customers look for the lowest cost to execute orders.

Lowering costs for customers, particularly futures commission merchants, is one goal of the CBOT-CME joint strategic initiatives committee. -Derivatives desk 312-408-8750;E-mail derivatives@reuters.com
